flags: Official cache documents a farming landscape and church architecture, but not curves, grades, travel time, road construction history or a designation campaign. Regional building history substitutes for unavailable road history; the final paragraph describes documented road connections without claiming a fully verified byway alignment.
The official brochure gives 38 miles and the truncated story map gives 38.4 miles. Used the brochure’s 38 miles without an invented hedge.

Dropped unsupported current claims: Brunner arrived from Switzerland in 1843; St. Henry’s $28,300 contract and $45,535 final cost; relics arrived from Rome in 1875; Minster’s clocks on all four sides and gold crosses. The church page instead gives approximately $100,000 for St. Henry, but cost is omitted.

Replaced the universal claim of a church at every crossroads in light of documented losses. The Maria Stein page records the May 29, 2025 destruction of St. John the Baptist; no reopening, replacement or current pilgrimage route is inferred.

Regional page says National Register additions occurred in 1976; individual church pages give 1979. Omitted the collective listing year. Maria Stein’s current fire account also supersedes older claims that St. John’s remains in use.
Preserved the existing moment coordinates as required, although St. Henry and Minster town-page coordinates differ. No current interior access is promised.
Overview remains shorter than 200 words because the official cache is thin on the drive itself; no grades, road conditions or journey time have been invented to fill it.
